messages:
Lina: Heads up — since the subnet-tagging + egress firewall tighten in eu-west-1 (rolled last night) we're seeing ~12% of GPU node provisions fail during bootstrap. error shows AssumeRole denied for node-role with Condition on 'aws:PrincipalTag/gpu'
Aj: Ugh. can you paste the failing log lines?
Lina: sure — snippet from controller logs: ```2026-03-19T22:04:13Z ERROR provisioner: assumeRole failed arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/node-role/i-abc123: AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole
StatusCode: 403
RequestID: xxxxx
Condition keys: aws:PrincipalTag/gpu != approved```
Satoshi: That condition bit smells like the new tag-boundary policy we pushed to subnets last week (az-affinity: enforce-tags). Did infra change the bootstrap role tags?
Maya: I pushed subnet policy, and also tightened egress to only allow privatelink/natgw to certain endpoints. I didn't touch node-role tags. But the bootstrap flow adds tags via the cloud-init assume. Could be a race where tags aren't set before STS call.
Ops-bot: :warning: warm-pool size decreased in eu-west-1 by 9% over last 30m (auto-scaling triggered). Alert ID: wp-eu-4023
Harry: From a security/compliance POV we can't open broad egress. But we can make a scoped exception for provisioning service and short-lived audit retention. Ingestion cost for full 90d retention in eu region would be ~€2.1k/mo for provisioning logs alone.
Lina: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) Add allow condition to IAM policy for the kube-bootstrap role to allow AssumeRole prior to tag assert (temporary) 2) Add egress allow to privatelink endpoint for provisioning service for 1 hour canary 3) Enable targeted audit retention (90d) for provisioning logs, downsample others to 7d 4) Backfill missing events if needed
Aj: Terraform snippet to patch the role policy (canary): ```resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "bootstrap-allow" { name = "bootstrap-assumerole-canary" role = aws_iam_role.node_role.id policy = jsonencode({ Version = "2012-10-17", Statement = [{ Effect = "Allow", Action = "sts:AssumeRole", Resource = "arn:aws:iam::111:role/bootstrap-target", Condition = { StringEquals = { "aws:RequestTag/gpu" = "pending" } } }] }) }```
Maya: I'll queue the egress exception + IAM patch as a canary to eu-west-1 only. Will also flip on a short-term retention rule for the provisioning log group (keeping raw for 30d instead of 90d across others).
Satoshi: Quick note on KMS — we had a key-alias rename during the rotation that left an alias mapping gap for the provisioning service. If provisioning tries to encrypt/decrypt with the old alias it will get InvalidCiphertext. Not an AssumeRole issue but related to bootstrap artifacts being KMS-encrypted.
Lina: good catch. can we route bootstrap through a fallback alias?
Maya: yes — I'll create alias 'alias/provision-eu-fallback' pointing to the active key and update the bootstrap config. Minimal blast radius.
Harry: Agree with canary path. Also we should capture audit events with high fidelity for the next 72h for forensic/compliance (store in cold storage after). I'll coordinate retention + cost estimates with finance.
Aj: After patching IAM + KMS alias I'll trigger a rolling warm-pool bump script: ```./scripts/warmup-bump --region eu-west-1 --count 20 --tag gpu=approved``` Will monitor Ops-bot alerts.
Ops-bot: :white_check_mark: canary patch pushed to eu-west-1 at 22:38Z, rolling 5 nodes through bootstrap.
Lina: early signs good, 5/5 succeeded. backfills showing the prior denied events are not appearing for the new nodes.
Satoshi: Once canary stable we should change the subnet tag enforcement to use a precondition that tolerates bootstrap timeframe (e.g., allow AssumeRole with RequestTag present). That avoids revert and keeps policy intent.
Maya: Agreed. Plan: canary → 1h observation → apply policy tweak + KMS alias fix → expand to rest of region. I'll file PRs and tag sec/reliability for review.
Harry: Also looping compliance team: they want a short writeup of the exception window and retention changes. I'll draft.
Lina: thanks. action items captured: Maya (egress canary + KMS alias + policy PR), Aj (IAM tf patch + warmup bump), Satoshi (policy condition suggestion), Harry (compliance + cost note). Will follow up with postmortem after 72h.
Sec-bot: Compliance checklist: https://internal.company/compliance/prov-audit-checklist — remember to update KMS key policy to allow DescribeKey for bootstrap service principal.
Aj: noted, making that change in the TF patch as well.
Maya: I'll close the canary if stable in 60m and then roll to all eu nodes. will ping here with final status.
Lina: Thanks team — keeping an eye on capacity metrics and will escalate if we see >5% sustained warm-pool decline.
